assessment: Two existing by-products offer testable reuse opportunities. Their existence is stipulated; their adequacy and causal contribution remain unproven. Neither opening alone establishes the 40-export success targets.

openings.claim: Can existing center schedules, including weekly handwritten annotations, supply enough dated evidence to reconstruct intended course membership for a requested week?
openings.delta: Reuse coordinator-maintained scheduling traces as a temporal test oracle for fabricated staging exports, turning after-download comparison into evidence for diagnosing selection errors.
openings.prediction: If these traces retain usable history, coordinators can independently distinguish a rename, an instructor reassignment, and a course split for the same requested week. If they contain only current names, this reuse fails.
openings.probe: In consenting coordinators’ sessions, inspect relevant traces inside authorized workspaces and record their source and update time. Ask coordinators to reconstruct dated course sets before seeing exports. Translate supported cases into fabricated staging fixtures and compare outputs; mark disagreements or missing history unresolved.
assumptions: Historical details are not established by the mere existence of schedules.
The bounded diagnostic exercise fits six engineer-days and existing staging capacity.
Attendance entry continues; the documented CSV remains supported.

openings.claim: An existing job-completion trace might also serve as a private replacement-file readiness signal, reducing coordinator waiting when a usable replacement is already available.
openings.delta: Give the completion trace a delivery-coordination role beyond recording execution and row totals.
openings.prediction: This helps only when completion-to-retrieval accounts for substantial delay; request-to-start delays or course-selection defects would remain.
openings.probe: For consented replacement requests, collect request, job-start, completion, and retrieval times within authorized workspaces. Verify whether completion can be securely associated with the correct center, requested week, and ready file. Trial a workspace readiness cue using fabricated data only if that association exists.
assumptions: Completion logs are supplied; request timestamps, artifact links, and center identifiers are not confirmed.
A readiness cue must not imply course-set correctness.
Proceed only if implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting without blocking attendance entry or changing the CSV schema.
